BEN-02.title: A binary replication label changes with precision alone, and one operator carries almost all of it
BEN-02.question: BEN-02 says replication is reported as a binary label that mixes estimand mismatch with random error. Holding the true trial-emulation discrepancy fixed, how much of the label is decided by precision rather than by the discrepancy, and which of the operators in use carries that sensitivity?
BEN-02.design: 16 structural scenarios crossing the true risk-difference discrepancy with trial and emulation precision, 10,000 replicates each, 480,000 benchmark pairs. Each replicate is one trial cohort and one emulation cohort with a binary outcome, scored by four agreement operators in current use. Truth is enumerated by exact summation over the covariate strata rather than by simulation, so the discrepancy each scenario carries is known to machine precision.
BEN-02.estimand: The probability that a pair-level agreement operator returns agreement, as a function of precision at a fixed true discrepancy, and the sensitivity S of that probability to precision alone
BEN-02.answer: The precision-conflation component is real and it is concentrated in one operator. Sensitivity S is 0.4915 against a threshold of 0.10 declared before the run, with a paired-bootstrap Monte Carlo interval of 0.4903 to 0.4931. Confidence-interval overlap carries essentially all of it at 0.4915; direction agreement carries 0.1244. Two benchmark pairs with the same true discrepancy can therefore be labelled agreeing and disagreeing on the strength of how precisely each was estimated, and the operator most used to produce the label is the one most exposed.
findings: The label moves with precision at fixed truth. Holding the true risk-difference discrepancy constant and varying only trial and emulation precision moves the probability of an agreement verdict by 0.49 on the interval-overlap operator, against a threshold of 0.10 set in the protocol before any result existed.

The exposure is not shared evenly. Direction agreement moves by 0.1244 over the same range, a quarter of the interval-overlap figure. An operator choice that is usually made for convenience decides most of the conflation.

It is not an estimation artifact. Coverage runs 0.944 to 0.956 against a nominal 0.95, maximum absolute bias is 0.00086, convergence is complete in every scenario, and the exact finite-cell summation used for truth agrees with itself to 2.2e-16. Nothing here is an estimator failing.
The bootstrap interval is narrow enough to matter. The Monte Carlo interval on S spans 0.0028, so the distance from the 0.10 threshold is not a Monte Carlo question.
BEN-02.not_answered: This is the pair-level component of BEN-02 and not the whole entry. It says nothing about between-pair heterogeneity across a benchmarking program, about calibration of a graded metric against a decision, or about the graded alternatives the catalog entry's own audit established already exist; the peer review named all three as scope this design does not cover, and they are declared limitations rather than results. Outcomes are binary at a single horizon, so the behavior of these operators on a time-to-event scale is untouched. The study measures how an operator behaves; it does not establish which operator a benchmarking program should adopt, because that depends on a decision the study does not model.
BEN-02.peer_review: Reviewed before running and returned unsound, with three fatal findings: the study answered a neighbouring question, the mechanism solved its eligibility parameter to produce the discrepancies it then measured, and the decision rule's negative branch was unreachable. All three were resolved in a revision pass, the first two by changing the design and the third by making both branches reachable from results the design can actually produce.

CNF-01.title: A single cumulative-initiation number at the horizon does not determine the attenuation it is asked to explain
CNF-01.question: CNF-01 asks authors to publish the cumulative incidence of initiation in both arms so a reader can see how far the contrasted strategies stayed distinct, and to quantify by simulation how much attenuation a given convergence rate produces. Does that diagnostic actually recover the attenuation?
CNF-01.design: Discrete monthly time to 10 years, 4000 individuals per replicate, confounded baseline initiation, later initiation in the comparator arm, and a treatment that works. 24 scenarios crossing three convergence rates, two timing shapes tuned to the same cumulative initiation at the horizon, initiation that does or does not concentrate in high-risk patients, and two effect-persistence regimes. 1000 replicates each, 24,000 replicates in all. Truth enumerated from the mechanism at two million individuals per scenario rather than estimated from the replicates.
CNF-01.estimand: Risk difference at horizons of 1 to 10 years for assignment to initiate at baseline versus not, with later initiation left to run, against the always-treated versus never-treated contrast the comparator arm would have supported had it stayed untreated
CNF-01.answer: No. Within the simulated grid, comparator-arm cumulative initiation at 120 months does not uniquely determine attenuation: matched early and late initiation scenarios, whose reported diagnostic agrees to within 0.0005, differ in attenuation by 0.0528 to 0.2027. Nine of the twelve matched pairs exceed the 0.05 threshold declared before the run by at least three Monte Carlo standard errors, at 5 to 46 of them; the other three sit within 3 and are individually inconclusive, and all three are at the lowest convergence rate, where there is least attenuation to misattribute. A single cumulative-incidence value at the horizon is therefore insufficient for recovering attenuation in these scenarios. What the reported number cannot see is when the comparator arm initiated and who initiated.
findings: The insufficiency scales with convergence, which is the opposite of reassuring. At 20 percent cumulative initiation the matched difference is 0.053 to 0.070 and only one of four pairs is established; at 45 percent it is 0.116 to 0.145 at 18 to 27 Monte Carlo standard errors; at 70 percent it is 0.181 to 0.203 at 39 to 46. The diagnostic is least informative exactly where attenuation is largest.

Attenuation is large and grows with the horizon. Pooled across scenarios its median is 0.024 at one year and 0.245 at ten, with a maximum of 0.567. A treatment that genuinely works can lose more than half its sustained-strategy effect to convergence alone.

Who initiates matters as much as when. Concentrating initiation in high-risk patients raises attenuation from 0.476 to 0.567 at the highest convergence rate while also inflating the reported diagnostic from 0.700 to 0.742, so the diagnostic moves in the right direction by the wrong amount.
Effect persistence is the one factor that barely matters. Transient and legacy regimes differ by less than 0.01 in attenuation throughout.

The estimators show small finite-sample bias rather than none. Coverage runs 0.934 to 0.970 against a nominal 0.95 and convergence is complete, but 14 of 288 cells carry bias beyond three Monte Carlo standard errors, to a maximum of 4.2. That does not touch the decisive comparison, which uses attenuation enumerated from the mechanism at two million individuals per scenario rather than estimated attenuation.
CNF-01.not_answered: The comparison holds the diagnostic fixed only at 120 months. At earlier horizons the early and late scenarios differ in observed cumulative initiation by as much as 0.269, so those contrasts are not comparisons at equal C(h) and cannot independently establish insufficiency there. The study establishes that C(120) alone is insufficient within this grid. It does not establish that reporting C is necessary, that the full initiation curve would be sufficient, or that a universal conversion from convergence to attenuation exists. The comparator arm converges upward and the treated arm never discontinues, so this is one direction of convergence only. There is no loss to follow-up and no competing event, both excluded so the attenuation is not confounded with a second mechanism. The scale is the risk difference throughout; a hazard ratio would mix this mechanism with non-collapsibility.
CNF-01.peer_review: Three rounds of results review, each in a fresh context that saw the catalog entry, the registered protocol and the result files but not the study's own summary. Round 1 returned uninformative with two fatal findings: the decisive quantity carried no Monte Carlo uncertainty, so its distance from the threshold could not be compared with its own error. Adding that uncertainty changed the finding, from twelve of twelve matched pairs clearing the threshold to nine. Round 2 returned three serious findings, one of which was an arithmetic error in the study's own reporting: bias was described as a share of the attenuation and computed against the risk difference, understating it by two orders of magnitude. Round 3 returned supported with three minor findings about claim strength, all folded into the wording above.
